meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: + accusative.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
A fact or a person.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: From Latin 'inspector' (observer, overseer, from 'inspicere', to look into).

examples.text: Инспекторы ищут нарушения только ради денег.
examples.trans: Inspectors look for violations only for money.
The inspector is checking the kitchen.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: A very polite request.

meanings.en: 'Будьте любезны' = would you be so kind

examples.trans: Would you be so kind as to call me.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'легал').
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: A door, a window. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть').

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Making a request.
Answer to thanks.
Handing something over.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить').

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.
You think he is testing us?

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: The milk is in the fridge.

examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

meanings.en: to get cold, feel chilled; to freeze solid
meanings.note: intransitive; past tense замёрз, замёрзла

examples.trans: Danya, are you cold or what?
Come on, get up, you'll freeze in the snow!

meanings.note: Удачи! = Good luck! (genitive: 'I wish you luck')

examples.trans: That's a real stroke of luck.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.
